# Carrier Layout Rule Sheet -- EEG-CAR-01 Rev C

**Document:** LAY-EEG-034  **Revision:** A  **Date:** 8 September 2026
**Issued by:** TI One Voice research programme (one.witysk.org), Brussels, Belgium
**Licence:** CC BY-SA 4.0
**Governing documents:** DSN-EEG-003 Rev C, then RFQ-EEG-001 Rev E, then ICD-EEG-006 Rev B.
**Generated by:** `tools/emit_rule_sheet.py` from `tools/rules.py`. The tables are not typed.

## 1. Scope and precedence

This sheet is the rule set for the placement and routing of **EEG-CAR-01 Rev C**, and it is **part of the order specification**. A departure from it is a layout error and is corrected at no charge, not a change request.

`tools/design.py` governs. Where this sheet and `design.py` disagree, `design.py` is right and this sheet is regenerated. Where this sheet and `kicad/EEG-CAR-01_RevC.kicad_dru` disagree, both are wrong until regenerated: they come from one source, `tools/rules.py`.

**Nothing in this package has been manufactured or measured, and no safety engineer has reviewed this design.**

## 2. Board and stack-up

The full specification is **DSN-EEG-003 Rev C section 3.2** and is not restated. The four lines a layout engineer needs:

- **150.0 x 130.0 mm**, rectangular, no cut-outs, no slots.
- **Four layers**: L1 signal, L2 reference plane, L3 reference plane, L4 signal. 1.60 mm +/- 10 % finished, FR-4 Tg >= 150 C, 1 oz outer and 0.5 oz inner copper, ENIG.
- **Through vias only**, 0.60 mm pad on a 0.30 mm finished hole, tented both sides. No blind, buried, back-drilled, filled or plugged via anywhere.
- Board floor **0.20 mm track / 0.20 mm clearance**, 0.25 mm copper to the board edge, 2.00 mm copper to a non-plated hole. Section 5 is stricter per class and section 5 wins.

## 3. Zoning and star points

**DSN-EEG-003 Rev C section 3.3 rules 1 and 2**, cited and not restated. In this sheet's terms:

- The board is two zones split at **x = 62.0 mm**: analogue left, digital right. No digital-class net may be routed into the analogue zone and no analogue-class net out of it. **One signal crosses by design** -- `CMP_RAW`, the comparator output, which must reach a 3.3 V GPIO and does so through R83 and the D23 clamp.
- `AGND_REF` is the analogue **0 V mid-rail and is not ground**. It is poured on L2 and L3 over the whole analogue zone; `DGND` is poured over the digital zone on the same two layers. L1 and L4 carry signals, which is why the board has four layers.
- **`AGND_REF` joins `DGND` at R90 and nowhere else. `HARN_SHIELD` joins `DGND` at R91 and nowhere else.** Both are 0 R 0603 parts and neither may become a copper bridge: each has to lift for a leakage measurement and refit. A second path of any kind, on any layer, is a layout error.

## 4. Isolation keep-out

**DSN-EEG-003 Rev C section 3.3 rule 4.** The strip **x >= 141.0 mm, y = 2.0 to 22.0 mm** carries **no copper on any of the four layers**, and no via, no pad and no footprint. It is `ISOLATION_KEEPOUT` in the board file and in the `.kicad_dru`.

The 2.5 kV barrier itself is **on the purchased ADuM4160 module at J10**, not on this board; nothing on the carrier is on the host side. What the carrier owes the barrier is to keep out from under the module's host half. **The rule is enforced against copper EDGES and not track centrelines**, which is what earlier revisions of this programme's own check got wrong.

## 5. Net classes

Eight classes over all **156** nets. **Minimum** is a floor and a conductor below it is an error; **preferred** is what to route at wherever the board allows it. `Vias` says whether the class may have one at all. `Confirm` marks a figure that is a proposal of this programme and not a transcription from a governing document -- if one of those is unroutable, say so at the placement gate rather than relaxing it silently.

| Class | Nets | Width min / pref (mm) | Clearance min / pref (mm) | Layers | Vias | Confirm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ELECTRODE` | 32 | 0.25 / 0.30 | 0.35 / 0.40 | F.Cu | NO | **yes** |
| `ANALOGUE_REF` | 5 | 0.30 / 0.40 | 0.20 / 0.30 | any | yes | **yes** |
| `POWER` | 8 | 0.40 / 0.80 | 0.20 / 0.30 | any | yes | no |
| `USB` | 2 | 0.30 / 0.30 | 0.35 / 0.35 | F.Cu | NO | no |
| `ANALOGUE` | 42 | 0.25 / 0.25 | 0.20 / 0.30 | any | yes | no |
| `LED_DRIVE` | 16 | 0.25 / 0.30 | 0.20 / 0.25 | any | yes | no |
| `DIGITAL` | 21 | 0.20 / 0.25 | 0.20 / 0.25 | any | yes | no |
| `DEFAULT` | 30 | 0.20 / 0.25 | 0.20 / 0.25 | any | yes | no |

Where the numbers come from:

- **`ELECTRODE`** -- Patient-connected. The 0.35 mm clearance is DSN-EEG-003 section 3.3 rule 3 and is not a proposal. The rest of this row IS a proposal: rule 3 says these nets are routed on L1 with the reference plane continuous beneath them, and a via breaks the plane it is routed over, so L1-only and no vias is what rule 3 means read literally. It is achievable -- the harness socket J14, the R/D/C protection rows and the module sockets J2/J4/J23/J29 are all on the top side. The 0.25 mm floor is above the board's 0.20 mm because Rev B only reached 0.20 mm on these nets by relaxing, and a patient-connected conductor is the last place to spend the last 0.05 mm. Current is not the constraint: these carry microamperes.
- **`ANALOGUE_REF`** -- AGND_REF, AVDD, AVSS and the module-2 pair. About 10 mA per rail (ICD-EEG-006 section 2.1), so 0.20 mm would carry it four times over: the width is for source impedance and for the mid-rail's noise, not for current. 0.40 mm preferred is what the Rev B router already aimed at.
- **`POWER`** -- VSYS, VBAT, V5V, VBUS_CHG, VBUS_IN, DVDD3V3, VDD_ISO, DGND. The worst case is about 610 mA at J13 (ICD-EEG-006 section 2.7, calculated). On 35 um outer copper at a 10 C rise, IPC-2221 gives about 1.29 A for 0.40 mm and about 0.89 A for 0.25 mm, so 0.40 mm is the floor with margin and 0.80 mm is the preferred width the Rev B router already used.
- **`USB`** -- DSN-EEG-003 section 3.3 rule 5, transcribed and not proposed: a 0.30 mm pair on 0.35 mm spacing on L1 directly over the DGND plane on L2, about 95 ohm differential. The width is the impedance, so it is a fixed value and not a minimum; a via would move the reference and is not permitted.
- **`ANALOGUE`** -- Envelope-detector nodes, the microphone and headphone paths, the comparator. Signal nets at high impedance; 0.25 mm is the board's preferred width and there is no reason for these to be narrower than that.
- **`LED_DRIVE`** -- 1.3 mA per site and 10.4 mA on the LED_V common (ICD-EEG-006 section 2.11, calculated), so current is nowhere near the constraint. These run to a harness connector and out of the box, which is the reason not to route them at the 0.20 mm floor.
- **`DIGITAL`** -- SPI, I2S, I2C, SDMMC, UART and the control lines. Logic-level, milliamperes.
- **`DEFAULT`** -- Everything the classes above do not name: test points, spare ways, no-connects, the harness screen, the button and reset lines.

The class of every net is in `kicad/EEG-CAR-01_RevC.kicad_pro` and, in a form a person can read, in `constraints/nets.md`.

## 6. Geometry rules

These are the seven findings an external layout engineer made against Rev B between 3 and 5 September 2026 (ECO-EEG-016 section 2, ECO-EEG-030), and they are why this sheet exists. **Six are rules; the seventh was a missing check and is section 7.** The right-hand column is not a formality: two of them KiCad cannot check, and this programme checks those itself on the geometry that comes back.

| # | Rule | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **No drill inside a pad.** No via inside an SMD pad or within 0.15 mm of one, on its own net or any other | KiCad DRC (`no_via_in_smd_pad`) **and** our DRC on return |
| 2a | **No dangling track end.** Every track end lands on a pad, a via, another track or a pour | KiCad DRC built-in `track_dangling`, raised to **error** in the project file, **and** our DRC on return |
| 2b | **No redundant copper path.** Not more than one copper path between the same two points on a net, outside a plane | KiCad DRC built-ins **and** our DRC on return |
| 3 | **45-degree routing.** No angle below 90 degrees between two segments of one track, and every segment on a 0, 45, 90 or 135 degree axis | **NOT CHECKABLE IN KiCad** -- there is no constraint for it. **Verified by our DRC on the returned board** |
| 4 | **Pad-centre entry.** A track entering a pad has its centreline within 25 % of the pad's minor dimension of the pad centre | **NOT CHECKABLE IN KiCad.** **Verified by our DRC on the returned board** |
| 5 | **Net classes.** Section 5 above: width, clearance, permitted layers and the via rule, per class | KiCad DRC (`width_*`, `clearance_*`, `layers_*`, `no_vias_*`) **and** our DRC on return |
| 6 | **Zoning, star points and the isolation keep-out.** Sections 3 and 4 | KiCad DRC through the rule areas **and** our DRC on return |

`kicad/EEG-CAR-01_RevC.kicad_dru` is the machine-readable half of this table and carries 37 rules. Load it with the project; it is not optional.

**Two more, from DSN-EEG-003 section 3.3, that are not new and are easy to miss.** Rule 7: **no via inside the outline of J2, J4, J23 or J29**, the analogue module connectors -- they are `NO_VIA_J*` rule areas in the board file. Rule 5: **`USB_DP` and `USB_DN` are a 0.30 mm pair on 0.35 mm spacing on L1 directly over the L2 DGND plane**, about 95 ohm differential. No coupon and no impedance report are required and none is wanted.

## 7. Placement

**Placement drives via count, must precede routing, and is reviewed before routing starts.** That is the reviewer's own principle and this programme has adopted it.

1. **The thirty connectors J1 to J30 are LOCKED**, with MH1-MH4 and FID1-FID3. The pod, the module plate MP-01 and the harness fix them and they may not move. **37 footprints are locked in `kicad/EEG-CAR-01_RevC.kicad_pcb` and the lock is the specification.** Everything else sits at its Rev B coordinate, unlocked, and is yours to place.
2. **Each of the sixteen protection networks is placed in a straight line -- resistor, then clamp, then filter capacitor -- running from the harness towards the module** (DSN-EEG-003 section 3.3 rule 3). The schematic is drawn that way so that the intent is visible: sheet `50_harness_input`.
3. **Envelope decoupling within 3 mm** of pins 4 and 11 of each OPA4376.
4. **Every electrode-class net is routed on L1 with the reference plane continuous beneath it.** That is what the `ELECTRODE` class's L1-only, no-via row in section 5 means, and it is DSN-EEG-003 section 3.3 rule 3 read literally.
5. **The placement stage is delivered as a `.kicad_pcb` with the STEP bodies loaded**, and it passes a 3D collision check with the module bodies installed before it is delivered. The bodies are in `mech/step/`.
6. **We confirm the placement before routing is confirmed.** The review is a written findings list by net, pad pair and coordinate, capped at four to six hours, under RFQ-EEG-002A as re-scoped by ECO-EEG-030.

**One open item that belongs to this programme and not to the layout contractor**, stated here because a placement reviewer will meet it: `mech/EEG-CAR-01_RevC_collision_check.txt` reports that the twelve modules do not fit on MP-01 -- 17 356 mm2 of declared envelopes into 12 409 mm2 of plate -- and that the plate's DevKit opening is 2 mm shorter than the DevKit. **Neither is a carrier layout question and neither blocks this order**; both are recorded in ASM-EEG-023 under MECH-D6-MODULE-ENVELOPES.

## 8. Deliverables expected back

1. **The KiCad project**, at the version agreed at the order -- `.kicad_pro`, `.kicad_sch` set, `.kicad_pcb`, and the `.kicad_dru` unchanged.
2. **A DRC run against this sheet**, clean, taken before handover, with the report. Sections 5 and 6 are the rule set; `.kicad_dru` is loaded.
3. **Gerber X2**, one file per layer, with file attributes.
4. **Excellon 2 drill files**, plated and non-plated separately.
5. **IPC-D-356A netlist** for the bare-board electrical test.
6. **CPL** for the surface-mount parts and, separately, the through-hole parts.
7. **Fabrication and assembly drawings.**

On return, this programme runs its own DRC over the geometry -- including rules 3 and 4 of section 6, which KiCad cannot check -- and grades the result. The tool is `tools/drc.py` with `tools/drc_geometry.py`, it is in the repository, and it is the same one that regraded Rev B and found 1 311 occurrences of these six rules in a board its own report called clean.
